model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, CET1 retention on risk-weighted-asset growth, AT1 and preference distributions charged in the flow

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: terminal nominal growth for a mature Chinese joint-stock bank (China nominal GDP ~4-5% less continued NIM drift), bracketed by revenue 5yr CAGR 1.7% and BVPS 5yr CAGR 6.3%; the DCF's base revenue path runs 3.5% -> 3.0%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Ordinary equity 3yr/5yr CAGR 9.6%/9.0% vs revenue 0.2%/1.7% and EPS 0.8%/5.0% (>30% apart). Equity growth is retained earnings plus the RMB40bn A-share convertible conversion in FY2024-25 (shares 48,935m -> 55,639m), not operating growth; per-share book compounds at 5-6%. Revenue stalled because NIM fell from 2.26% (FY2020) to 1.62% (H1 2026) while the balance sheet grew ~6%/yr. Equity CAGR is NOT used as the growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are null: a bank's reported FCF (OCF - capex) is deposit-flow noise (-182bn FY2024, +405bn FY2025). The relevant series is net profit attributable to ordinary shareholders: 63,788 (FY2024) -> 66,784 (FY2025), +4.7%, with H1 2026 attributable profit +3.1%. Ordinary equity FY2020-FY2025 from the kpis table; BVPS 9.60 -> 13.01 RMB. Dividend payout 28.1% (2022) -> 31.75% (2025) of ordinary profit.

scenario_narratives.base: NIM stabilises at ~1.6%, credit cost ~1.0%, operating income grows 3-3.5% and RWA growth slows from 7% to 3%. FCFE rises from ~RMB17bn (FY2026E, below the dividend) to ~RMB60bn by FY2036 as capital retention falls; terminal ROE ~8%, terminal P/B ~0.7x. CET1 held at 9.4% throughout.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Chinese credit cycle turns: NIM recovers 5-10bp, credit cost falls below 0.9%, cost-to-income ~30%, RWA growth 3.5-5%. FCFE ~RMB35bn in FY2027 rising to ~RMB70bn; terminal ROE ~9.6%; payout can rise above 30%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Credit cost spikes to ~1.5% on property/LGFV/retail losses while NIM compresses toward 1.4%; profit falls ~15%; RWA keeps growing on policy lending so FCFE is ~RMB3-5bn for two years, far below the dividend. Either the dividend is cut or a discounted capital raise dilutes; terminal ROE ~5.8%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is worth the equity cash flow it can distribute after funding its own capital requirement, discounted at the cost of equity. For China CITIC Bank that flow is net profit to ordinary shareholders (after tax, NCI, preference dividends and perpetual-bond coupons) less the equity retained to hold CET1 at 9.4% on growing risk-weighted assets. Today that FCFE (~RMB17bn) is below the ~RMB24bn the Bank pays out, so the headline 5.3% dividend yield is partly financed by capital-ratio drift; the model credits only the FCFE and lets it rise as RWA growth decelerates. Net debt is zero by construction; deposits are operating funding. The H share trades at 0.54x book; the model's base terminal P/B is ~0.7x, consistent with a ~8% ROE at a 10.5% cost of equity.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit cycle: retail stress is building (credit-card NPL 2.62%, personal consumer loan NPL 2.80% up 0.66pt, retail segment PBT nearly halved in FY2025) alongside property and LGFV exposure that management flags as key risk areas; a return to the FY2019-20 credit cost of 1.6-1.8% takes the pre-tax margin to ~30% and FCFE to zero (bear case).

Capital: CET1 9.37% at H1 2026, down 35bp in 18 months with the dividend exceeding FCFE; a discounted recapitalisation (state or CITIC Group) would dilute H-share holders - the flat share count does not model it.
NIM: 2.26% (FY2020) to 1.62% (H1 2026); further LPR cuts without matching deposit repricing resume the compression (bear revenue path).
Policy-directed lending ('Five Priorities') allocates RWA to state objectives rather than return; RWA grew 8.7% in FY2025 on 2.5% loan growth.

Governance and currency: 64.75% CITIC Financial Holdings control, no buyback lever, payout set by policy (~30%); RMB flows against an HKD quote - a 10% RMB move is a 10% move in the HKD value; 10% H-share dividend withholding tax is not modelled.

Sell-side (Citi HKD 9.78, JPM 8.75, HSBC 8.60, Mar-Jul 2026) sits below this base case: the gap is the base case's assumption that RWA growth decelerates to 3% and CET1 can be held at 9.4% without a raise; if RWA keeps growing 7-9% the bear path is the right one.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (0998.HK, HKD) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 6.50-8.695. FX CNYHKD=X, USDCNY=X, USDHKD=X and 601998.SS from the same API on the same date.
data_sources.financials: 0998.HK_Metrics.csv / metrics_normalized (FY2017-FY2025 annual, H1 2022-H1 2026 interim, RMB millions) built from the HKEX annual reports and interim reports in Extracted/; kpis table for RWA, CET1, NIM, NPL, coverage, credit cost, ordinary shareholders' equity, BVPS, dividends. FY2025 annual report: EPS note (net profit to ordinary shareholders 66,784; other-equity-instrument distributions 3,834), capital adequacy table (RWA 7,684,339), dividend table (payout 31.75%), outlook p.105. H1 2026 interim: capital table (CET1 9.37%, RWA 8,033,562, lines 1868-1874), interim dividend (RMB2.03/10 shares, 30.04% payout, line 5682-5685), share count 55,645,162,264 (line 5684), NIM 1.62% (line 365).
data_sources.qualitative: 0998.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-12), read after the drivers were set and before the final build; it confirmed them (asset growth ~5%, payout >=30%, retail NPL stress, H1 impairment +21.5%). Outlook and risk context also taken directly from the FY2025 annual report MD&A (outlook 2.12, credit-card NPL 2.62% line 2790, consumer-loan NPL 2.80% line 2772) and the H1 2026 interim.

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E operating income, RMB m: H1 2026 actual 110,409 (interim p.341, +4.7% YoY) + H2 2026E 110,400 (FY2025 H2 actual 107,210 x 1.03). FY2025 actual 212,636. Revenue = net interest income + net fee and commission income + other non-interest income, the Bank's 'operating income' line.
inputs.share_count_basis: 55,645,162,264 A + H ordinary shares on the register at 30 June 2026 (interim p.5684); one class, same economic rights, so the per-share value applies to the H share. Held FLAT: the A-share convertible bond that lifted the count from 48,935m to 55,639m over FY2024-25 has fully converted/matured (Mar 2025); preference shares convert only on a CET1 trigger (5.125%), not modelled; SBC-zero. A state or CITIC Group recapitalisation at a discount to book is the dilution risk the flat count ignores (see notes).
inputs.debt_cash_note: Bank: deposits (RMB6.05tn), interbank funding, central-bank borrowings and debt securities issued (RMB1.09tn at 30 Jun 2026) are operating funding, and cash/central-bank balances are liquidity, not surplus. Net debt is zero by construction on the FCFE route; nothing is bridged after the flows.
inputs.fcf_note: last_fcf is FY2026E FCFE = net profit attributable to ORDINARY shareholders 67.6bn (PBT 85.0bn at 38.5% margin, less income tax, NCI and other-equity-instrument distributions at 20.5%) LESS capital retained to hold CET1 at 9.4% on 7% RWA growth (0.07 x 0.094 x 7,684,339 = 50.6bn). Reported OCF - capex (FY2025: 443,082 - 37,820 = 405,262) is deposit and interbank flow noise and is not used.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero: no share-based payment scheme disclosed in the FY2018-FY2025 annual reports (ShareRepurchases 0 every period, StockBasedComp 0 in the CSV); basic = diluted EPS (RMB1.20 FY2025). House and street bases coincide; band_position is degenerate.
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate converts CNY (model; the Bank reports in RMB) to HKD (H-share quote): CNYHKD=X 1.1721 at 2026-10-09T13:38Z, Yahoo Finance. Triangulated against USDCNY=X 6.6922 / USDHKD=X 7.8472 = 1.1726 (same source, 2026-10-09). The Shanghai A share (601998.SS) closed at CNY 9.00 = HKD 10.55, a ~25% A/H premium that is normal for Chinese banks, so the dual listing is not a parity check. Per-share values are per ordinary share and apply equally to A and H shares.
inputs.fy0: FY2026E (year ending 2026-12-31, unreported: H1 2026 actual + H2 estimate)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:06Z HKEX regular close (Friday); valuation dated the following Monday
inputs.cet1_anchor: CET1 ratio 9.37% on RWA RMB8,033,562m at 30 Jun 2026 (interim p.1868-1874); 9.48% on 7,684,339m at FY2025; 9.72% on 7,068,736m at FY2024. Net CET1 capital 752,516m. Leverage ratio 7.01%.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single CNY cost of equity 10.5% in every scenario (risk is charged once, through the scenario weights, not by moving the discount rate). Built in the flows' own currency: 10-year China Government Bond ~1.8% (ASSUMPTION: not fetched; the PBOC easing cycle has had the 10Y CGB in the 1.6-2.0% range since 2025) + beta ~1.05 x China ERP ~6.5% = ~8.6%, plus ~1.9pt for risks a CSI-300 ERP does not price for an H-share holder in a JOINT-STOCK bank: thinner CET1 buffer than the Big Four (9.37% vs ~12-14%, ~1.4pt above the D-SIB minimum, and drifting down 35bp in 18 months because the dividend exceeds FCFE), credit cost 1.05% in H1 2026 against credit-card NPL 2.62% and personal-consumer-loan NPL 2.80% (FY2025, up 0.66pt), state-directed lending under the 'Five Priorities', majority CITIC Group/CITIC Financial Holdings control (64.75%) with no buyback lever, and capital-account/RMB convertibility risk. One point above the 9.5% used for the sibling 0939.HK (CCB) this week; the differential is the joint-stock-bank premium. Hurdle for entry price is the house 15%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Bank: IFRS 16 right-of-use depreciation and lease-liability interest (RMB10,249m lease liabilities at FY2025, AR line 12158) sit inside operating expenses, i.e. inside the pre-tax margin. lease_cost_pct_path is zero so the charge is not taken twice; nothing is deducted as debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, inside the 'cash_tax_rate' deduction: the margin is calibrated to PROFIT BEFORE TAX (84,043 FY2025, after credit impairment 57,939) and the deduction rate covers income tax (12,553; 14.9%), profit attributable to non-controlling interests (872; 1.0%) and distributions on other equity instruments (3,834; 4.6% - preference dividends 1,428 + perpetual-bond coupons 1,680 + 726). FY2025 total 20.5% = (84,043 - 66,784) / 84,043, where 66,784 is net profit attributable to ordinary shareholders (AR FY2025 EPS note, line ~14348). Other equity instruments (RMB104,948m) and NCI (18,817m) are therefore NOT deducted again in a bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> dcf-methods routing row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker, thrift'. Run as FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, the house precedent for banks (HSBC, LYG, WF, MFG, HDB, IBN, BMO, USB, WFC, NAB.AX; 0939.HK this week). First valuation of this ticker, no MEMORY.md entry. Not an owner-FCF DCF: deposits are operating funding, OCF is meaningless (swings from -341bn to +443bn), net debt is zero by construction and no debt or cash is bridged. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = operating income; ebitda_margin = pre-tax profit margin (after credit impairment, which is the real cost of a bank); sbc, D&A, leases and working capital all zero; cash_tax_rate = income tax + NCI + AT1/preference distributions, so EBIT x (1 - rate) = net profit to ORDINARY shareholders; capex = equity retained to hold CET1 at 9.4% on RWA growth (g_RWA x 9.4% x prior-year RWA, as % of revenue), so FCF = FCFE = distributable earnings. Terminal growth applies to FCFE at the cost of equity; terminal_cap_multiple 18x FCFE is above the Gordon multiple in every scenario (13.7x base, 14.8x bull, 12.8x bear) and does not bind. KEY FINDING: FY2026E FCFE ~RMB17bn is BELOW the ~RMB22-24bn of ordinary dividends plus AT1/preference coupons the Bank pays; the gap is why CET1 fell from 9.72% (FY2024) to 9.37% (H1 2026). The dividend is being funded by capital-ratio drift, and the valuation credits only the FCFE, which ramps as RWA growth slows from ~7-9% to ~3%. QUALITATIVE CONTEXT: 0998.HK_Analysis.json was absent when the drivers were first set and landed before the final build; it was read and CONFIRMS the drivers without moving any path (FY2026 guidance: total asset growth ~5%, payout no less than 30%, 'stabilise NIM' with no numeric target; H1 2026 net profit roughly flat ex one-off gains; sell-side targets HKD 8.60-9.78 in Mar-Jul 2026, i.e. below this base case and around the weighted value). The drivers rest on the FY2025 annual report (outlook p.105: stability and risk control, 'Five Priorities', advanced-approach capital measurement) and the H1 2026 interim (NIM 1.62%, -1bp YoY, first stabilisation after four years of compression from 2.26%; NPL 1.15% flat; coverage 203%; credit cost 1.05% vs 0.89% FY2025; cost-to-income 26.4% H1; attributable profit +3.1%; interim dividend RMB2.03/10 shares = 30.04% payout). Revenue has been flat for four years (FY2021 204.6bn -> FY2025 212.6bn, 1.0% CAGR) while RWA grew ~5-9%/yr, so NI/RWA is 0.83% and falling; ROE 9.65% H1 2026 vs 11.6% FY2017. The H share trades at 0.54x H1 2026 BVPS (RMB13.42) and a 5.3% FY2025 dividend yield. Valuation date is 9.5 months into FY2026, so FY2026E is fy0 (not discounted) and the first discounted flow is FY2027; the FY2025 final dividend (10.74bn, May 2026) and FY2026 interim (11.30bn, Dec 2026) are paid out of fy0 and are not double-counted.

bear.growth_rationale: NIM resumes compressing toward 1.4% (further LPR cuts, deposit costs sticky), fee income flat; revenue repeats the FY2021-25 stall.
bear.margin_rationale: Credit cost rises to ~1.5% in FY2027-28 (property developers, LGFVs, retail credit cards) - the FY2019-20 margin was 29.6-30.1% at credit cost 1.6-1.8% - then partly recovers to 34%.
bear.capex_rationale: Policy-directed lending keeps RWA growing 7.0, 6.0, 5.0, 5.0, 4.5, 4.0, 3.5, 3.0, 2.5, 2.5% while earnings fall; CET1 held at 9.4% consumes almost all of ordinary profit in FY2027-28 (FCFE RMB3-5bn against a ~RMB20bn dividend). In practice this is the scenario where the dividend is cut or a discounted recapitalisation dilutes the H share; the flat share count understates the damage. Terminal ROE ~5.8%.
bear.tax_rationale: Fixed AT1/preference coupons against a smaller PBT.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon 1.025/0.08 = 12.8x FCFE; cap does not bind.
bear.narrative: A credit-cost cycle plus continued NIM compression. Earnings fall ~15%, the capital ratio cannot support both growth and the dividend, and value accrues to the state's lending priorities rather than minority H-share holders.

base.growth_rationale: Operating income +3.5% for four years then 3.0%: NIM stabilising at ~1.6% (H1 2026 -1bp YoY after -64bp over four years), balance sheet growing ~5% slowing to 3%, fee income flat-to-up (H1 2026 +1.9%). Below RWA growth, so NI/RWA keeps drifting down.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax margin after credit impairment. FY2023 36.4%, FY2024 37.9%, FY2025 39.5%, FY2026E 38.5% (H1 42.5% vs 44.2% a year earlier as credit cost rose to 1.05%; H2 is seasonally ~5pt lower). Base holds 38.5-39%: credit cost ~1.0%, cost-to-income ~32%, no NIM recovery.
base.capex_rationale: Equity retained to hold CET1 at 9.4% on RWA growth of 5.5%, 5.0, 5.0, 4.5, 4.0, 4.0, 3.5, 3.5, 3.0, 3.0 from FY2026E RWA RMB8,220bn (FY2025 7,684bn, H1 2026 8,034bn). RWA grew 5.1% FY2024, 8.7% FY2025, 4.5% in H1 2026; the FY2025 annual says the Bank will 'enhance the application of advanced capital measurement approach', which lowers RWA density over time. Retention / revenue: 0.055 x 0.094 x 8,220,000 / 228,528 = 18.6% in FY2027, falling to 11.1% as RWA growth converges on terminal growth. Terminal-year equity ~RMB1,154bn on RWA 12,281bn; terminal ROE ~8.1%.
base.tax_rationale: Income tax 14.9% (FY2025; FY2024 14.1%, low because of tax-exempt government-bond interest) + NCI 1.0% + other-equity-instrument distributions 4.6% = 20.5% of PBT, held flat. Coupons on RMB70bn perpetual bonds and RMB35bn preference shares are fixed in RMB, so the percentage falls slightly as PBT grows; ignored (conservative).
base.terminal_note: Gordon on FY2036 FCFE at 10.5% - 3.0% = 13.7x; the 18x cap does not bind in any scenario. It binds only in the sensitivity grid's 8.5% cost-of-equity row (Gordon 18.7x at g=3%), which is the cap doing its job: a bank earning ~8% on equity is not worth 19-22x its distributable earnings. Implied terminal P/B ~0.7x on terminal ROE ~8.1%, consistent with (ROE - g)/(CoE - g).
base.narrative: Steady-state joint-stock bank: NIM holds ~1.6%, credit cost ~1.0%, RWA growth decelerates from 7% to 3% and the dividend becomes fully covered by FCFE around FY2028-29. No recapitalisation needed; CET1 held at 9.4%.

bull.growth_rationale: NIM recovers 5-10bp as deposit repricing completes and the PBOC easing cycle ends; fee income grows mid-single digits (wealth management, custody); balance sheet grows ~5%.
bull.margin_rationale: Credit cost back to 0.8-0.9%, cost-to-income to ~30%, property book stabilises; 42% is roughly the FY2025 H1 annualised margin.
bull.capex_rationale: CET1 held at 9.4% on RWA growth of 5.0, 4.5, 4.0, 4.0, 3.5 then 3.5% (advanced-approach RWA savings). Terminal ROE ~9.6%.
bull.tax_rationale: Fixed AT1/preference coupons fall to ~4% of a larger PBT.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon 1.035/0.07 = 14.8x FCFE; cap 18x does not bind.
bull.narrative: China's credit cycle turns, NIM and credit cost both improve, RWA growth slows to 3.5% and the payout ratio can rise above 30% without eroding CET1.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 35% (above the house default and above the 30% used for 0939.HK/CCB): CITIC Bank is a joint-stock bank with CET1 ~1.4pt above its D-SIB minimum and drifting down because the dividend already exceeds FCFE; credit cost is rising (1.05% H1 2026 vs 0.89% FY2025; H1 loan impairment +21.5% YoY); credit-card NPL 2.62% and personal-consumer-loan NPL 2.80% with retail segment pre-tax profit nearly halved in FY2025 (RMB9.23bn -> 5.30bn); revenue has been flat four years. Bull 20%: NIM has only just stopped falling and the policy-lending mandate caps upside. Base 45%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
